title: Runtime exec-context histogramming and NVTX throttle markers for kernel-level attribution
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Build a low-noise, high-signal telemetry layer that attributes hot kernels to execution contexts without overwhelming NVTX ranges or trace storage. We will implement lightweight exec-context histogramming, NVTX "throttle" markers for long-running kernels, and a sampled mapping between GPU stream IDs and request IDs to reconstruct per-request kernel timelines for expensive (P0/P1) workloads.

Background: Current profiling emits dense NVTX ranges and fully expanded trace spans for every kernel. This provides signal but saturates the tracing pipeline and increases S3/BigQuery storage by ~3x for production workloads. We need an approach that preserves the ability to debug latency regressions and identify kernel selection regressions, but reduces telemetry volume and CPU/GPU-side overhead.

Deliverables:
- Exec-context histograms aggregated per-worker: count, p50/p95/p99 latency, kernel name fingerprint, and GPU stream id (for sampled traces).
- NVTX throttle markers: emit a compact "throttle" NVTX range when a kernel exceeds dynamic threshold (per-kernel adaptive threshold based on sliding-window median). Throttle ranges compress with a special envelope so tracing backends can collapse them.
- Sampled span collector: 1 in 200 requests (configurable) captures full span chain including NVTX ranges, kernel fingerprints, and stream->request mapping. Samples should be biased toward requests with high token latencies.
- Dashboard: per-model and per-route histograms, a dry-run metric showing percentage telemetry reduction, and a reconstructed-sampled-request timeline view.
- Backwards-compatibility: old NVTX naming preserved for sampled spans to avoid breaking existing dashboards.

Acceptance criteria:
- End-to-end overhead on production CPU/GPU telemetry < 1.5% (measured over 72h A/B).
- Tracing/observability storage cost for telemetry reduced by at least 60% with default sampling and throttle thresholds.
- Ability to reconstruct sampled request timelines with >=95% kernel-to-request mapping fidelity.
- Dashboard surfaces kernel-choice regressions and attention-path anomalies for 3 real workload predicates.

Trade-offs and decisions discussed:
- Sampling frequency vs fidelity: we prefer adaptive sampling (bias toward slow requests) to keep low storage while preserving debugging capability.
- NVTX throttling vs loss of granularity: throttle ranges will carry a compressed fingerprint so we can still identify which kernel was throttled even if durations are aggregated.
- On-device vs off-device aggregation: exec-context histograms will be aggregated in-process to reduce metrics cardinality, with periodic flush to the control plane. This increases code complexity but lowers trace volume.

Test plan:
- Unit tests for fingerprint hashing to ensure deterministic kernel keys across builds.
- Integration test that simulates bursty attention patterns and verifies throttle markers are emitted.
- Canary A/B on dedicated pool with 1% traffic, monitor telemetry overhead and sample reconstruction accuracy.

Rollout plan:
- Feature-flag behind runtime-profiling-v2 toggle.
- Stage 1: Dry-run instrumentation on prod (no throttle markers emitted, only histogram counts).
- Stage 2: Enable throttle markers and 0.5% sampling.
- Stage 3: Increase sampling to 0.5-1% and enable dashboarding.

Monitoring and KPIs:
- telemetry.overhead.cpu_pct and telemetry.overhead.gpu_pct (target <1.5%).
- tracing.storage.reduction_pct (target >=60%).
- sample.reconstruction.fidelity_pct (target >=95%).

Notes on implementation details:
- Kernel fingerprinting: use XXH3_128 over kernel binary id + input-shape signature + quantization-profile tag. Keep the output hex-encoded (8 bytes) to reduce cardinality.
- Adaptive threshold: per-kernel sliding window median (5 min) * 3 = throttle threshold, with a floor set per model-class (e.g., 0.2ms for tiny ops).
- NVTX envelope: add a compact envelope header with type="throttle" and fingerprint field so compressed ranges can be expanded server-side for sampled traces.
- Stream mapping: add a short-lived mapping table (stream_id -> sampled_request_id) with TTL 2s, emitted only for sampled requests to avoid state explosion.

Risks:
- If sliding-window parameters are too aggressive we may hide short regressions. Mitigation: conservative defaults and a "capture once" slow-request trigger.
- Fingerprint drift across runtime builds if binary metadata changes. Mitigation: include build-id in fingerprint and map build-id in control-plane to previous fingerprints where possible.

Next steps:
- Spike: implement histogram aggregator + NVTX envelope prototype (owner: Marco Ruiz).
- Obtain review from Observability (SRE) and Kernel team on envelope format.
- Create PR for runtime flags and default config.
